advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In _record_at, verify `rev^{commit}` resolves (rev-parse --verify) before treating a failed `git show` as a missing record; raise PublishSwapError when the revision is unresolvable
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_publish.py:108: shown = run_git(root, "show", f"{rev}:{compat.COMPAT_FILENAME}", check=False)
src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_publish.py:109-111: if shown.returncode != 0: # No record yet: the implicit legacy store, which has no epoch. return {"format_version": ..., "required_capabilities": []}

src/rebar/_store/compat.py:187-196: the sibling _remote_store_epoch notes `git show ref:path` uses the same non-zero status for a missing path and an unreadable ref and resolves the ref separately with rev-parse --verify
Rollback calls stamp_superseding_epoch(shadow, BACK, replaced_tip=<rewritten tip>); the rewritten tip may not exist in a fresh shadow clone that was reset to the backup tip
advisory.finding: _record_at treats any non-zero `git show <rev>:.rebar-compat` as 'no record yet' (the legacy store with no epoch), including when `rev` itself does not resolve. A mistyped or missing `replaced_tip` therefore makes stamp_superseding_epoch silently write lineage [null] instead of the real lineage. That breaks rollback supersession proof for clones on the rewritten baseline.
scenarios: Operator rolls back from a shadow cloned from the backup ref, which does not contain the rewritten tip object: the record becomes {epoch: BACK, epoch_lineage: [null]}, so clients on NEW fail remote_epoch_supersedes_local and get DIVERGED instead of being overridden back
advisory.suggested_fix: On a non-zero `git show`, run `run_git(root, 'rev-parse', '--verify', f'{rev}^{{commit}}', check=False)`. If that also fails, raise PublishSwapError(f'{rev} does not resolve in the shadow'). Only return the legacy record when the revision resolves but the file is missing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the S3 upload/delete phase so a failure raises PublishSwapError naming the rollback prefix and the keys still present, and either removes new_key (restoring the T0 set) or tells the operator not to let the doctor run
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_publish.py:222: _put_bundle(root, s3, ref, new_tip, new_key)
src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_publish.py:224-225: for key in deleted: s3.s3.delete_object(Bucket=s3.bucket, Key=key)
src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_publish.py:49-50: class PublishSwapError: "A publish step failed; the message says whether anything was written."
src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:115: the doctor heals whenever len(bundles) > 1, folding every head into the published ref
Absence: no try/except around the put/delete sequence and no rollback/compensation of new_key on failure
advisory.finding: The S3 swap uploads the new bundle and then deletes the originals one by one, with no handling for a partial failure. If an upload or a delete raises midway (S3/network error), the ref is left holding the new bundle plus some or all of the old ones. That is the multi-bundle state the auto-doctor folds into a lossless merge, which resurrects the rewritten-away history. The raw boto/git exception also does not say what was already written, despite PublishSwapError's contract.
scenarios: delete_object for the second original fails transiently: the ref now has {new_tip.bundle, T0.bundle}; the next client fetch triggers heal_multi_bundle, which merges T0's history back into the published tip

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In `_swap_bundles_locked`, before returning, re-list `s3.get_bundles_for_ref(ref)` and fail loudly unless it is exactly `[new_key]`. Also refresh the lock, or check it is still owned, before the delete phase, so a lock broken for staleness during the long copy/upload can't let a concurrent bundle survive or be silently mixed in.
evidence: Shared resource: the ref's bundle set `f"{s3.prefix}/{ref}/{new_tip}.bundle"` and its siblings under `<prefix>/<ref>/`, as listed by `s3.get_bundles_for_ref(ref)` (reclaim_publish.py `_swap_bundles_locked`).
Executor 1: `publish_s3_bundle_set` -> `lock_key = s3.acquire_lock(ref)` -> `_swap_bundles_locked(...)` (reclaim_publish.py:196 and the try block after it).

Executor 2: any other writer of the same ref under the same helper lock, e.g. the auto-doctor `lock_key = s3.acquire_lock(ref)` at src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:94 followed by `_publish_and_prune` (s3_doctor.py:131), or a client git-remote-s3 push through the helper's per-ref lock.

Lock lease semantics, as modelled for the helper in tests/integration/s3_doctor_harness.py:137-139: `age = time.time() - lp.stat().st_mtime` / `if age > self.lock_ttl_seconds:` / `lp.unlink(missing_ok=True)`, then it re-acquires. Default `lock_ttl_seconds: int = 60` (s3_doctor_harness.py:102).

`release_lock` deletes the lock with no owner check: `self._lock_path(remote_ref).unlink(missing_ok=True)` (s3_doctor_harness.py:149). The swap's `finally: s3.release_lock(ref, lock_key)` can therefore delete a lock now held by the writer that broke the stale one.
Interleaving READ: `keys = [b["Key"] for b in s3.get_bundles_for_ref(ref)]` and the check `if heads != expected:`, both at the start of `_swap_bundles_locked`.

Interleaving WRITE window after that read: `_copy_object(...) for key in keys` (download plus put of each full T0 bundle), `_put_bundle(root, s3, ref, new_tip, new_key)` (git init/push/bundle create/put_object), then `for key in deleted: s3.s3.delete_object(Bucket=s3.bucket, Key=key)`, where `deleted` comes only from the stale `keys`. Nothing re-lists after the deletes and nothing re-checks the lock.

Harm: a bundle written by the concurrent writer after the stale lock was broken is not in `keys`, so it survives next to `new_key`. The ref ends up with two or more bundles, and the doctor's `if len(bundles) <= 1:` noop check (s3_doctor.py:115) no longer applies. The doctor then folds the T0-descended head back in, which the module docstring says the adapter must prevent: 'its auto-doctor folds divergent heads back in ... which would resurrect the rewritten-away history'.
Not prevented by any guard: the module has no lock refresh or renewal, no check after the writes that `get_bundles_for_ref(ref)` returns exactly `[new_key]`, and no owner check on release.
advisory.finding: publish_s3_bundle_set holds the per-ref S3 lock across a long critical section: it downloads and re-uploads every full-history T0 bundle, then builds and uploads the new one. It never checks whether the lock expired (the helper lock modelled in the harness expires after a TTL) and never re-reads the bundle set before reporting success. A concurrent git-remote-s3 push or doctor heal that breaks the stale lock can add a bundle descended from T0 after the T0 check. The swap then deletes only its own pre-read `keys`, so that bundle survives next to the new tip. The next auto-doctor run merges the rewritten-away history back, which is the outcome this adapter exists to prevent. The swap also returns a successful BundleSwap.
scenarios: A reclaim of a large store: copying several full-history T0 bundles and uploading the new one takes longer than the helper's lock TTL. Meanwhile a client runs `rebar` auto-push to the same S3 ref. The helper sees a stale lock, breaks it, and uploads `<sha>.bundle` descended from T0. The swap then deletes only the originals it listed earlier and reports success. On the next fetch, the doctor merges T0 history back on top of the reclaimed baseline.
advisory.suggested_fix: After the deletes, re-enumerate `s3.get_bundles_for_ref(ref)`. If any key other than `new_key` is present, raise a PublishSwapError that says the bundle set was modified concurrently and names the rollback prefix, so the operator re-runs from the backups rather than trusting the swap. Where the helper allows it, re-check or refresh lock ownership right before the first write and right before the delete loop. Do the large `_copy_object` downloads before taking the lock if possible, keyed to the T0 sha set and re-verified under the lock, so the hold stays well under the TTL.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the store_epoch_problem docstring in src/rebar/_store/compat.py to state that differing epochs are also compatible when the remote record's epoch_lineage names the local epoch.

src/rebar/_store/compat.py:203-205 (unchanged docstring of the same function): 'An absent record and a present record with no epoch both describe the pre-reclaim store and are compatible; otherwise epochs must be equal opaque strings.'

docs/documentation-policy.md:16: Comments are a living reference whose canonical source is 'The comment beside the relevant code', and their correction method is 'Update or remove the comment with the code'.

docs/concurrency.md:839-841 (changed) documents the new rule: 'compat.store_epoch_problem lets them merge their unpushed writes as usual, because the restored record's lineage names their epoch.' The docstring contradicts this.
advisory.finding: The docstring of store_epoch_problem still says that, apart from the absent-record and no-epoch cases, 'epochs must be equal opaque strings'. The changed code now also allows a union across different epochs when the remote record's epoch_lineage names the local epoch. The docstring describes a contract the function no longer enforces.
scenarios: A developer reads the store_epoch_problem docstring to learn when sync or push refuses a union. They conclude that differing epochs are always refused, and miss the lineage exception that rollback re-convergence depends on.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the last sentence of the docstring at src/rebar/_store/compat.py:203-205 to say that epochs must be equal opaque strings, or that the remote record's epoch_lineage must name the local epoch (the reclaim-rollback case in ADR 0106 §6). Without one of these, the guard refuses the union.

reclaim_publish.py `_swap_bundles_locked`: `backed_up = tuple(_copy_object(...) for key in keys)` then `_put_bundle(root, s3, ref, new_tip, new_key)` then `s3.s3.delete_object(...)`. These writes run in sequence, with no rollback between them.

tests/integration/test_reclaim_publish_s3.py: the only abort tests are `test_bundle_swap_aborts_without_writing_when_heads_moved` and `test_bundle_swap_aborts_when_the_ref_lock_is_held`, and both fail before any write.
Named call sequence: patch `remote.s3.put_object` to raise on the key `f"{remote.prefix}/tickets/{new_tip}.bundle"`. No test checks that the original bundle keys survive and the lock is released.
advisory.finding: Some new error and legacy branches in reclaim_publish have no tests. `_record_at` has a no-record fallback that returns the implicit legacy store, which should stamp lineage `[None]`, plus non-JSON and non-object errors. `_raise_push_failure` has a `PublishSwapError` branch for push failures that are not lease rejections. Only the moved-remote `PublishAborted` path is tested.
merged_from: No test injects a failure partway through the S3 bundle swap, such as `put_object` failing for the new bundle after the rollback copies were written. So nothing checks what an operator is left with in that case: the originals still present and the rollback copies intact. The tests only cover aborts that happen before the first write.
scenarios: A legacy store with no compat record is reclaimed. If the stamp left `None` out of the lineage, legacy clones could not prove they were superseded, and no test would catch it.
An unreachable remote is misreported as 'remote moved', telling the operator to recompute the reclaim when the real problem is connectivity.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the S3 bundle swap fail safe: if any step after `_put_bundle` fails, delete the new bundle (or otherwise stop the doctor from folding the set) and raise PublishSwapError saying exactly what was written.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_publish.py:222: `_put_bundle(root, s3, ref, new_tip, new_key)` uploads the new bundle before any original is removed

src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_publish.py:224-225: `for key in deleted: s3.s3.delete_object(Bucket=s3.bucket, Key=key)` has no try/except or rollback; an exception here (S3 error, credential expiry, network failure) propagates after the new bundle is already published

No error handling in _swap_bundles_locked removes new_key or restores a single-bundle state when a later step fails, and the exception that escapes is a raw botocore error, not PublishSwapError, so the operator is not told that something was written
src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:114-115: `_heal_locked` heals any ref with `len(bundles) > 1`

src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:240-241: `if _git(base_path, "merge-base", tip, head_ref).stdout.strip() == "": extra = ["--allow-unrelated-histories"]` means the doctor will union the parentless reclaimed tip with the old T0 head
The module docstring (reclaim_publish.py lines 11-15) says the doctor 'would resurrect the rewritten-away history' and that the adapter must replace the set exclusively
advisory.finding: If publish_s3_bundle_set fails partway through (after the new bundle is uploaded but before every original is deleted), it leaves a multi-bundle set and does nothing to clean it up or mark it. The next s3_doctor auto-heal sees more than one bundle and folds the rewritten-away T0 history back into the new tip using --allow-unrelated-histories. That breaks the guarantee this adapter exists to provide: that the replaced history is never merged back.
scenarios: During the swap, delete_object for the first original bundle fails (throttling, expired STS token, network drop). The lock is released in the finally block, and the next client fetch/push triggers heal_multi_bundle, which merges T0's history back into the reclaimed tip and publishes the combined bundle.
init_remote_head raises after the deletes; the set is in a valid state, but the caller gets a raw exception with no word on whether anything was written.
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap the steps after `_put_bundle` (deletes and init_remote_head) in try/except. On failure, try to delete `new_key` so the set goes back to the originals, which are also backed up under rollback_prefix. Then raise PublishSwapError listing which keys were written or deleted and pointing to rollback_prefix, so the operator recovers by hand before any doctor run.
